group.title: Feelings and character
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: Worried and nervous about something.
examples: She felt {anxious} before the exam.
wrong: He was anxious because everything was perfect and he had nothing to worry about.

words.meaning: Sure of yourself or of what you can do.
examples: He felt {confident} about the interview.
wrong: She felt confident because she was sure she would fail.

words.meaning: Eager to learn or know something.
examples: The children were {curious} about the box.
wrong: She was curious about nothing and wanted to know nothing.

words.meaning: Sad because something was not as good as you hoped.
examples: I was {disappointed} with my test result.
wrong: She was disappointed because the result was better than she dreamed.

words.meaning: Feeling shy or uncomfortable in front of other people.
examples: He felt {embarrassed} when he forgot her name.
wrong: He was embarrassed because everyone praised him and he loved it.

words.meaning: Very happy and full of energy about something.
examples: The children are {excited} about the trip.
wrong: She was excited, so she fell asleep at once and did not care.

words.meaning: Annoyed because you cannot do or change something.
examples: I felt {frustrated} when the computer froze.
wrong: She was frustrated because everything went smoothly.

words.meaning: Feeling thankful for something kind that someone did.
examples: I am {grateful} for your help.
wrong: I am grateful, so I never say thank you.

words.meaning: Unhappy because you want what someone else has.
examples: He was {jealous} of his friend’s new car.
wrong: She was jealous because she was glad for her friend and wanted nothing.

words.meaning: Sad because you have no friends or company.
examples: She felt {lonely} in the big city.
wrong: He felt lonely because there were fifty friends around him all day.

words.meaning: A little afraid or worried about something that will happen.
examples: I always feel {nervous} before a presentation.
wrong: I felt nervous because I was sure everything would be fine and I was fully calm.

words.meaning: Pleased about something you or someone else has done.
examples: Her parents were very {proud} of her.
wrong: He was proud because he had done something shameful.

words.meaning: Happy because something bad did not happen.
examples: I felt {relieved} when the test was over.
wrong: She felt relieved when the bad news got worse.

words.meaning: Feeling worried and tired because of too much pressure.
examples: He felt {stressed} before the deadline.
wrong: She is stressed because she has nothing to do and is fully relaxed.

words.meaning: Feeling that something was not expected.
examples: I was {surprised} to see her there.
wrong: I was surprised because I knew everything in advance.

words.meaning: Unhappy or worried because of something that has happened.
examples: He was {upset} about the news.
wrong: She was upset, so she laughed and sang all day.

words.meaning: Slightly angry about something.
examples: She was {annoyed} when he arrived late.
wrong: He was annoyed because the bus came early and was delighted.

words.meaning: Very surprised, often in a good way.
examples: We were {amazed} by the size of the castle.
wrong: She was amazed by the small building she had seen a hundred times.

words.meaning: Happy and positive.
examples: The waiter was {cheerful} all day.
wrong: She is cheerful because she is very sad and cries.

words.meaning: Quiet and relaxed; not worried.
examples: Stay {calm} and speak slowly.
wrong: He stayed calm by shouting and running around.

words.meaning: Happy to give money, time or help.
examples: He is very {generous} with his time.
wrong: She is generous because she never gives anything to anyone.

words.meaning: Telling the truth; not cheating.
examples: She is an {honest} person.
wrong: He is honest because he always tells lies.

words.meaning: Having good manners.
examples: It is {polite} to say please and thank you.
wrong: He is polite because he shouts at his friends.

words.meaning: Not polite.
examples: It is {rude} to talk with your mouth full.
wrong: He is rude because he always says please and thanks.

words.meaning: Nervous or uncomfortable with other people.
examples: He is {shy} and does not speak in class.
wrong: He is shy because he loves speaking to a huge crowd.

words.meaning: Caring only about yourself.
examples: It was {selfish} of him to take all the cake.
wrong: He is selfish because he shares everything with others.

words.meaning: Refusing to change your mind.
examples: He is too {stubborn} to say sorry.
wrong: She is stubborn because she always changes her mind at once.

words.meaning: Wanting to be very successful.
examples: She is an {ambitious} young lawyer.
wrong: He is ambitious because he wants nothing in his life.

words.meaning: Good at thinking of new ideas.
examples: She is very {creative} and paints beautiful pictures.
wrong: He is creative because he copies every idea exactly.

words.meaning: Someone or something you can trust to work well.
examples: She is a {reliable} friend.
wrong: He is reliable because he forgets everything and is often late.

words.meaning: Easily hurt or upset by what people say.
examples: He is very {sensitive} to criticism.
wrong: She is sensitive because nothing ever upsets her.

words.meaning: To believe that someone is honest and will not hurt you.
examples: I {trust} my best friend.
wrong: I trust him because he lied to me many times.

words.meaning: To stop being angry with someone who did something wrong.
examples: I can {forgive} him for forgetting my birthday.
wrong: I forgive her when I am still very angry and will not talk.

words.meaning: To say that you are sorry.
examples: I want to {apologize} for being late.
wrong: I apologize when I want to blame the other person.

words.meaning: To say that you are unhappy about something.
examples: Customers often {complain} about the long wait.
wrong: I complain when I am happy with the service and tell everyone.

words.meaning: A kind thing you say to praise someone.
examples: She gave me a nice {compliment} on my English.
wrong: A compliment is a rude thing you say to hurt someone.

words.meaning: To respect and like someone for what they do.
examples: I {admire} her courage.
wrong: I admire him because I find him boring and weak.

words.meaning: To feel sorry about something you did.
examples: I {regret} saying those words.
wrong: I regret it, so I am glad that I did it.

words.meaning: Able to wait calmly without getting angry.
examples: The teacher is very {patient} with young children.
wrong: He is patient because he shouts when he waits for one minute.

words.meaning: The way you feel at a particular time.
examples: She is in a good {mood} today.
wrong: A mood is a place where you buy clothes.

words.meaning: A strong feeling such as love, fear or anger.
examples: She showed no {emotion} when she heard the news.
wrong: An emotion is a machine that makes toast.
